use_cases.name: Run the leave accrual job
use_cases.goal: Credit every eligible employee's leave entitlement for the period exactly once, as defined by the accrual policy bound to the employee's leave band.

stakeholders.interest: Sees the correct entitlement on the day it falls due, without raising a ticket.
Avoids manual credits and the year-end clean-up that double credits cause.
Encashment, loss-of-pay and F&F figures depend on balances that are never overstated.
Every credit traces to a policy version, a run and an idempotency key.

use_cases.trigger: Nightly scheduler; the 1 January annual credit date; an employee reaching the end of the EL eligibility wait.
preconditions: An accrual policy (client set LP-01 to LP-12) is published and bound to each leave band (RL-170).
Each active assignment carries a leave band, a worker class and an employment start date.
The leave ledger enforces a unique index on the idempotency key (person, leave type, period, transaction type).
postconditions_success: Exactly one credit row exists per person, leave type and period, carrying source_ref to the policy and the run.
leave.credit.posted has been emitted for each new row and the projected balance reflects it.
The run log records counts of tuples selected, credited, skipped as not eligible and skipped as already posted.
postconditions_failure: No partial credit for a person and period is committed; the failed tuples are listed in the run log.
A re-run of the same period creates only the missing rows and never a second credit.

main_flow.action: Select eligible (person, leave type, period) tuples from the accrual policy bound to each employee's leave band.
Check whether the band's EL eligibility wait has been served (standard band: no EL in the first six months of service).
Write one credit row per person, type and period with a unique idempotency key and emit leave.credit.posted.
Apply band values: AGM and above get 18 EL, 6 CL and 6 SL on 1 January; others 1.5 EL monthly plus 6 CL and 6 SL in January.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee is in the standard band and has not completed six months of service.
steps: The platform posts no EL credit for the tuple and records the reason 'eligibility wait not served'.
CL and SL tuples for the same person continue to be processed.
alternate_flows.rejoin: Returns to step 3 for the remaining tuples

alternate_flows.condition: The employee completes six months of service on the run date.
steps: The platform posts a single 9-day EL catch-up credit instead of six monthly accruals (RL-171).
From the next monthly run the employee receives the standard 1.5 EL accrual.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee is a trainee.
steps: The platform reads the trainee type from the employee record.
DET and GET trainees receive CL on the trainee scheme; other trainee types receive no CL unless the scheme states otherwise (BS:RL-13).
alternate_flows.rejoin: Returns to step 4 for the remaining leave types

exception_flows.condition: The job is re-run for a period already credited (restart or manual re-trigger).
exception_flows.handling: The unique idempotency key rejects the duplicate insert; the tuple is logged as already posted and no second credit is written.

exception_flows.condition: An active employee has no leave band or the band has no bound accrual policy.
exception_flows.handling: The tuple is skipped, no default credit is posted, and an HR operations task is raised naming the employee and the missing binding.

exception_flows.condition: A storage failure interrupts the batch.
exception_flows.handling: The per-person transaction rolls back; the next run resumes from the failed tuple and the idempotency key prevents duplicates.

nfrs: The nightly accrual for 10,000 active employees completes within 15 minutes.
Three consecutive re-runs of the same period leave the ledger row count unchanged (property test TC-PR08).
Every credit row is attributable to a policy version and run identifier, retained for the life of the employment record plus the statutory retention period.
use_cases.frequency: Nightly, plus the 1 January annual credit

user_stories.want: senior-grade employees to receive their full annual entitlement automatically on 1 January
user_stories.so_that: they can plan the year without HR keying credits by hand

acceptance.then: 18 EL, 6 CL and 6 SL are credited in one movement with source_ref naming the band policy

use_cases.name: Prorate casual and sick leave for a new joiner
use_cases.goal: Give each leave-eligible new joiner CL and SL credits proportional to the joining month, posted to the ledger with the proration rule as the source.

stakeholders.interest: Has usable CL and SL from the first week of employment.
Does not compute proration by hand for every hire.
Maintains the proration table as data rather than code.

use_cases.trigger: A hire is completed and the employee's assignment becomes active.
preconditions: The proration table (dataset sheet 16_Leave_Proration) is configured on the leave scheme.
The hire record carries the joining date and the worker class.
postconditions_success: Prorated CL and SL credits are posted with source_ref citing the proration rule (RL-181).
leave.credit.posted is emitted and the joiner's projected balance shows the credits.
postconditions_failure: No credit is committed for an ineligible worker class or a joining date without a proration row.
An HR operations task explains why no credit was posted.

main_flow.action: On activation of the new joiner's assignment, look up the CL and SL proration band for the joining month.
Prepare the prorated CL and SL credits with the proration rule as source_ref, for posting with leave.credit.posted.
Confirm the worker class is leave-eligible before commit; contract, third-party, consultant and gig classes receive no credit.

alternate_flows.condition: The worker class is not leave-eligible.
steps: The platform discards the prepared credits; nothing is written to the ledger.
The hire record shows 'Not leave-eligible by worker class' on the leave tab.

alternate_flows.condition: The joiner is a trainee.
steps: The platform applies the trainee band's policy; DET and GET trainees receive CL, other trainee types do not unless the scheme says so (BS:RL-13).
alternate_flows.rejoin: Use case ends with the trainee credits committed

exception_flows.condition: The joining date is after 4 December, for which the proration table holds no row.
exception_flows.handling: No CL or SL credit is posted; an HR operations task cites the missing row. The entitlement follows the client's answer to the open question recorded against T-14 and is loaded as a table row before go-live.

exception_flows.condition: The hire activation event is delivered twice.
exception_flows.handling: The idempotency key on (person, type, period, transaction type) rejects the second credit.

nfrs: Proration credits are visible to the joiner within 5 minutes of assignment activation.
Proration values are held only in configuration; a table change needs no code release.

user_stories.want: CL and SL for new joiners to be prorated from the joining-month table automatically
user_stories.so_that: every joiner gets the same treatment without manual calculation

acceptance.given: E1060 Jayanthi Elangovan joined on 06 April 2026 in a leave-eligible class
acceptance.then: 4 CL and 4 SL are credited with source_ref citing the proration rule

acceptance.given: employees join on 15 January and 2 December 2026
acceptance.then: they receive 6 CL and 6 SL, and 1 CL and 1 SL, respectively

user_stories.want: workers in non-eligible classes to receive no leave credit at all
user_stories.so_that: contract and gig workers are not shown balances they cannot use

acceptance.then: no CL or SL credit is written and the leave tab shows 'Not leave-eligible by worker class'

acceptance.then: 3 CL is credited on the trainee scheme

user_stories.so_that: no entitlement is granted that the client has not confirmed

acceptance.then: no CL or SL credit is posted and an HR operations task names the missing table row

acceptance.given: the client's answer has been loaded as a row for 5 to 31 December
acceptance.then: the credit from that row is posted once

use_cases.name: Apply for leave with rule validation
use_cases.goal: Let an employee apply for leave and receive an immediate, rule-named decision on whether the request can enter the approval chain.

stakeholders.interest: Learns at the time of applying, not days later, whether the request breaks a rule.
Receives only requests that already satisfy balance, combination and cap rules.
Policy is enforced consistently and the blocking rule is named in every rejection.

use_cases.trigger: The employee opens Apply for leave (SCR-030) on mobile, web or the business messaging channel and submits a request.
preconditions: The employee holds an active assignment with a leave-eligible worker class.
Leave types, combination rules and monthly caps are configured on the leave scheme.
postconditions_success: The leave_request is in VALIDATED state and is handed to the approval chain (LVE-04).
leave.request.created has been emitted.
postconditions_failure: The request is in REJECTED_BY_RULE with leave.request.rejected_by_rule emitted and the blocking rule named to the employee.
No approval instance is created and no ledger row is written.

main_flow.action: Enter leave type, from and to dates, half-day flags, reason and contact during leave, then submit.
Project the balance from the ledger as at the leave start date, honouring per-credit expiry, and show it with expiry warnings.
Check the combination rule: is CL being taken with, or merged into, EL or SL across the contiguous absence?
Check monthly caps: would the request exceed 2 CL or 10 EL in a calendar month, counting days already approved?
Check conflicts with team calendar, holidays, rest days and existing attendance, then set the request to VALIDATED.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee applies without connectivity on mobile.
steps: The app queues the request locally and shows it as 'Queued'.
On reconnection the request is submitted and validation runs against the ledger at that moment.

alternate_flows.condition: The conflict check finds a biometric Present status on a requested date.
steps: The platform shows the conflicting attendance record rather than resolving it silently.
The employee amends the dates, or proceeds and the conflict is carried to the approver as a visible flag.
alternate_flows.rejoin: Returns to step 5 or proceeds to the approval chain

exception_flows.condition: The projected balance at the start date is lower than the days requested.
exception_flows.handling: Submission is blocked with the projected balance and any credits expiring before the start date shown.

exception_flows.condition: CL is contiguous with EL or SL, including where they were applied for separately.
exception_flows.handling: The request moves to REJECTED_BY_RULE before the chain starts; the message names the combination rule.

exception_flows.condition: The request would exceed the monthly cap of 2 CL or 10 EL.
exception_flows.handling: The request moves to REJECTED_BY_RULE; the message names the cap and the days already counted in that month.

nfrs: Validation result is returned within 1.5 s at p95 on mobile and web.
Rejection messages name the rule in the employee's selected language.

user_stories.want: to see my balance as it will stand on my leave start date, including credits that will expire first
user_stories.so_that: I do not apply for days I will not have

acceptance.given: I hold 4 comp-off days of which 2 expire on 20 October 2026
acceptance.when: I start an application for comp-off from 25 October 2026
acceptance.then: the screen shows a projected balance of 2 days and flags the 2 expiring days

acceptance.given: my projected EL on 1 November 2026 is 3 days
acceptance.when: I apply for 4 EL days from 1 November
acceptance.then: submission is blocked and the projected balance of 3 days is shown

user_stories.want: a request that breaks the CL combination rule to be refused at once with the rule named
user_stories.so_that: I can re-plan instead of waiting for an approver to reject it

acceptance.given: 2 CL for 10 and 11 June 2026 are approved for E1019
acceptance.when: E1019 applies for 3 EL from 12 to 14 June 2026
acceptance.then: the request is set to REJECTED_BY_RULE and the message names the CL combination rule

acceptance.given: LV-2026-0802 for E1019 combines CL and EL
acceptance.then: no approval instance is created

user_stories.want: monthly caps to be enforced at validation with the counted days shown
user_stories.so_that: I understand exactly why the request failed

acceptance.when: I apply for 1 more CL day in June
acceptance.then: the request is blocked at the third CL day and the message names the cap of 2 CL a month

use_cases.name: Approve leave through the three-level chain
use_cases.goal: Route a validated leave request through Supervisor, HOD and HR Head in strict order and, on approval, debit the ledger against the specific credits consumed.

stakeholders.interest: Gets a timely decision and sees who approved at each level.
Acts only on requests in their own subtree, in turn.
Receives a payroll input for approved leave that affects pay.
Each step is recorded with actor, decision and timestamp.

use_cases.trigger: A leave request reaches VALIDATED state.
preconditions: A chain definition for leave exists, resolved by request type, worker class and location (RL-010).
Supervisor, HOD and HR Head are resolvable for the applicant's reporting line.
postconditions_success: The request is APPROVED; the ledger debit references the credits consumed (RL-195).
Attendance and team calendar show the leave and a payroll input is raised; leave.request.approved is emitted.
postconditions_failure: On rejection the request is REJECTED with no ledger movement and the employee is notified with the approver's comment.

main_flow.action: Start the sequential chain Supervisor, HOD, HR Head, each with its SLA, and set the request to PENDING_APPROVAL.
Each approver decides in turn on the approvals inbox; a rejection at any step ends the request.
On final approval, debit the ledger against the credits consumed, update calendar and attendance, and raise the payroll input.
Where needed, edit or close the request at any stage with a mandatory reason; the change is logged with actor and time.

alternate_flows.condition: An approver rejects the request.
steps: The platform sets the request to REJECTED and closes the remaining steps.
The employee is notified with the approver's comment; no ledger row is written.

alternate_flows.condition: A step's SLA elapses without a decision.
steps: The platform reminds the approver and escalates as defined in the chain definition.
The request stays at the same step; later steps do not open early.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee cancels while the request is pending.
steps: The platform sets the request to CANCELLED and withdraws open approval tasks.

exception_flows.condition: The HR Head or HOD attempts to approve before the preceding step has decided.
exception_flows.handling: The action is blocked; the inbox shows which step is pending.

exception_flows.condition: The resolved approver is the applicant.
exception_flows.handling: The step is not offered to the applicant; it is routed to the next authority in the chain definition.

exception_flows.condition: The credits referenced at validation were consumed or lapsed before final approval.
exception_flows.handling: The balance is re-projected; if insufficient, the debit is not written and the request returns to HR operations with the shortfall shown.

nfrs: An approval decision is reflected in the next approver's inbox within 5 s.
Approval history for a request is retained and viewable for at least the statutory retention period.

user_stories.want: the chain to stop me approving before the Supervisor and HOD have acted
user_stories.so_that: the client's three-level policy cannot be bypassed

acceptance.given: a leave request is pending at the Supervisor step
acceptance.when: the HR Head opens it and selects Approve
acceptance.then: the action is blocked with the message 'Pending at Supervisor'

acceptance.given: Supervisor and HOD have approved
acceptance.then: the request is APPROVED and the history shows three entries, each with actor and timestamp

user_stories.want: to approve or reject a team member's leave from my inbox with a comment
user_stories.so_that: my decision and reason reach the employee immediately

acceptance.then: the request becomes REJECTED, the employee is notified with the comment and no ledger debit exists

acceptance.then: the ledger shows a debit of 3 EL referencing the credits consumed

user_stories.so_that: exceptions can be handled without losing the audit trail

use_cases.name: Record early return and re-credit unused leave
use_cases.goal: Release the unused days of an approved leave when the employee returns early, crediting the balance and correcting attendance in one atomic change.

stakeholders.interest: Gets unused days back and is paid for the days actually worked.
The payslip, attendance and leave ledger agree; closed runs are not rewritten.
The reversal references the original debit.

use_cases.trigger: An employee on approved leave reports back for work before the approved end date.
preconditions: The leave request is APPROVED and the ledger debit references the credits consumed (RL-195).
The actual return date lies within the approved span.
postconditions_success: The request is in EARLY_RETURN; a reversal row references the original debit and leave.credit.reversed is emitted.
Released days are recomputed to Present or their punch-derived status.
Where a released date sits in a locked payroll period, an arrears request exists for the next open run.
postconditions_failure: Neither the reversal nor the recompute is committed; the request remains APPROVED and the user sees the failure.

main_flow.action: Record the actual return date inside the approved leave span on Apply for leave and emit leave.early_return.recorded.
In one transaction, write a reversal row referencing the original debit and queue attendance recompute for the released dates.
Recompute the released dates so they become Present or their punch-derived status; emit time.attendance_day.recomputed.
Check whether any released date falls inside a locked payroll period.

alternate_flows.condition: A released date lies in a payroll period whose inputs are locked or whose run has closed.
steps: The platform raises payroll.arrears.requested for the next open run with the person, period and reason.
The closed run is left unchanged.

alternate_flows.condition: A released date has no punch and is not a rest day.
steps: The day takes its punch-derived status (for example Absent) rather than Present, and the employee is notified to regularise it.

exception_flows.condition: The entered return date is before the leave start or after the approved end date.
exception_flows.handling: The entry is refused with the approved span shown.

exception_flows.condition: Either the reversal write or the recompute enqueue fails.
exception_flows.handling: Both are rolled back; no reversal exists without its recompute, and the user is asked to retry.

exception_flows.condition: The request is still pending approval.
exception_flows.handling: Early return is not offered; the user is directed to amend or cancel the pending request.

nfrs: Reversal and recompute complete within 60 s of recording the return for a 30-day span.
The reversal and recompute enqueue are atomic; fault-injection tests show no state where one exists without the other.

user_stories.want: to record an early return and have the unused days credited back and marked present together
user_stories.so_that: the balance and the attendance never disagree on the payslip

acceptance.given: 10 days of EL from 1 to 10 October 2026 are approved

acceptance.then: a reversal of 4 EL referencing the original debit is written and 7 to 10 October are marked Present

acceptance.given: the recompute enqueue fails during the same transaction
acceptance.then: no reversal row exists and the request remains APPROVED

user_stories.so_that: a run that has been paid is never reopened

acceptance.when: the return is recorded on 2 October
acceptance.then: payroll.arrears.requested is raised for the October run and the September run totals are unchanged

acceptance.given: no released date falls in a locked period
acceptance.then: no arrears request is raised

user_stories.so_that: I can confirm the days came back

acceptance.when: she opens the leave balance and ledger
acceptance.then: the original debit and the reversal credit appear as linked entries

acceptance.given: the reversal is posted
acceptance.when: the projected EL balance is read
acceptance.then: it has increased by exactly the released days

use_cases.name: Credit, consume and lapse compensatory off
use_cases.goal: Grant comp-off for approved rest-day or holiday working with its own 60-day clock, consume it earliest-expiring first and lapse whatever remains on its own expiry date.

stakeholders.interest: Knows exactly when each comp-off day expires and loses none early.
Comp-off liability is accurate per credit, not estimated at balance level.
Each lapse row names the run that wrote it.

use_cases.trigger: Approval of rest-day or holiday working; a comp-off availing; the nightly lapse job.
preconditions: The comp-off leave type carries expiry_days (client value 60), with any employee-level lapse window held on the employee or scheme (BS:RL-06).
Rest-day or holiday working has been approved through the time module.
postconditions_success: Each credit carries expires_on = credit date + lapse days; consumption references the earliest-expiring open credit.
Unconsumed days are lapsed by one Lapse row per credit on its own expiry date, with leave.compoff.lapsed emitted.
postconditions_failure: A failed lapse run writes nothing for the affected credit; the next nightly run lapses it with the original expiry date.

main_flow.action: On approved rest-day or holiday working, credit comp-off with expires_on = credit date + 60 days; emit leave.compoff.credited.
When comp-off is availed, draw from the earliest-expiring open credit first; emit leave.compoff.consumed.
Nightly, write a Lapse row for each credit past expires_on with days remaining; emit leave.compoff.lapsed.
Keep each credit's clock running across the leave-year boundary; the year end never truncates it.

alternate_flows.condition: The days availed exceed the earliest open credit.
steps: The platform consumes that credit fully and takes the remainder from the next-earliest credit, writing one consumption row per credit.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee record holds its own lapse window.
steps: The platform uses the employee-level lapse days instead of the leave-type default when setting expires_on.

exception_flows.condition: The lapse job runs twice for the same date.
exception_flows.handling: The idempotency key per person, credit and date prevents a second Lapse row.

exception_flows.condition: A comp-off request exceeds the open credits projected at its start date.
exception_flows.handling: Validation blocks the request with the expiring credits listed.

exception_flows.condition: Year-end processing attempts to lapse open comp-off credits.
exception_flows.handling: Comp-off is excluded from year-end lapse; each credit lapses only on its own date.

nfrs: The nightly lapse job processes 50,000 open credits within 10 minutes.
An employee notice is sent 7 days before any comp-off credit lapses.
use_cases.frequency: Nightly lapse; per event for credit and consumption

user_stories.want: each comp-off day to carry its own 60-day expiry
user_stories.so_that: a later credit is not lost because an earlier one expired

use_cases.name: Process leave year end and birthday leave
use_cases.goal: At year end carry forward, encash or lapse each leave type as the scheme defines, raise encashment as a payroll input, and credit birthday leave in its own window.

stakeholders.interest: Receives the correct encashment and understands which days lapsed.
Receives encashment as an input computed on the statutory wage base.
Can preview year-end figures before they are written.

use_cases.trigger: 31 December year-end schedule; an employee's birthday eligibility window opening.
preconditions: Year-end treatment per leave type is configured (EL carry-forward cap; CL and SL lapse).
The target payroll run for encashment exists for the period (PAY-01).
postconditions_success: EL within the cap is carried forward, the excess encashed; CL and SL closing balances are lapsed; leave.yearend.processed is emitted.
An encashment payroll input exists in the named run; birthday leave credits are posted with their own window.
postconditions_failure: A failed commit writes no year-end rows for the affected employee; a re-run produces the same figures as the preview.

main_flow.action: At year end, carry EL forward up to the carry-forward cap, encash the excess, and lapse CL and SL; emit leave.yearend.processed.
Raise the encashment as a payroll input in the named run, valued on the statutory wage base; emit payroll.input.raised.
Credit birthday leave within its own eligibility window; emit leave.credit.posted.

alternate_flows.condition: HR operations runs year end in Preview mode first.
steps: The platform computes carry-forward, encashment and lapse per employee without writing.
HR operations reviews the preview and selects Commit; the committed figures equal the preview.
alternate_flows.rejoin: Returns to step 1 in commit mode

alternate_flows.condition: The scheme's EL carry-forward cap is configured as 0, as in the client's acceptance test.
steps: All closing EL is encashed; nothing is carried forward.

exception_flows.condition: The named payroll run has already locked its inputs.
exception_flows.handling: The input is not added to the locked run; it is raised to the next open regular run and HR operations is notified.

exception_flows.condition: The year-end job is re-run after a partial failure.
exception_flows.handling: Idempotency keys prevent a second encashment or lapse row for any employee already processed.

exception_flows.condition: The employee's separation date falls before the birthday window opens.
exception_flows.handling: No birthday credit is posted.

nfrs: Preview and Commit for 10,000 employees each complete within 20 minutes.
Preview and Commit figures match to the half day and to the paisa for every employee.

user_stories.want: to preview year-end results before committing them
user_stories.so_that: errors are caught before any balance or payroll input is written

user_stories.want: my birthday leave credited in its own window
user_stories.so_that: I can take it without using my EL

acceptance.given: my birthday is 14 March and the client's window is configured on the leave type
acceptance.then: one birthday leave day is credited with leave.credit.posted emitted

acceptance.given: the window has closed without use

use_cases.name: View projected leave balance and its ledger trail
use_cases.goal: Give employees and HR a balance computed from the ledger as at any date, together with the transactions that produced it.

stakeholders.interest: Can answer 'why is my balance 6.5' without raising a ticket.
Uses one projection for the apply screen, the assistant, the payslip and the F&F.
Balance is reproducible from ledger rows alone.

use_cases.trigger: Any read of a leave balance: the balance screen, the apply screen, the assistant, the payslip or the F&F.
preconditions: The requester is the employee, or HR within scope, or an agent with a declared balance tool.
postconditions_success: The balance as at the requested date is returned with the contributing ledger rows.
postconditions_failure: Out-of-scope requests are refused and logged; no partial data is returned.

main_flow.action: Project balance = credits − debits − lapses − encashments + reversals, as at the requested date.
Show on the balance and ledger screen the transactions behind the balance, each with date, type, days and source reference.

alternate_flows.condition: The requested date is in the future.
steps: The projection excludes credits whose expires_on falls before that date and includes scheduled accruals already posted.

alternate_flows.condition: HR operations exports the ledger for an employee in scope.
steps: The platform produces the export with the same rows shown on screen and logs the export.

alternate_flows.condition: The mobile app is offline.
steps: The last synchronised balance and ledger are shown read-only with the sync time.

exception_flows.condition: A user requests the balance of an employee outside their scope.
exception_flows.handling: The request is refused and an access event is recorded.

exception_flows.condition: A component attempts to read a stored balance column.
exception_flows.handling: No such column exists; all reads go through the single projection function.

nfrs: Balance projection returns within 300 ms at p95 for a ledger of 500 rows.
The same projection function serves all consumers; a consistency test compares apply-screen, payslip and F&F values for 1,000 employees.

user_stories.want: to see every transaction that makes up my balance
user_stories.so_that: I can verify it myself

acceptance.given: my EL ledger has credits of 13.5, a debit of 6 and a reversal of 2 for 2026
acceptance.when: I open the leave balance and ledger
acceptance.then: the balance shows 9.5 and each of the three entries with its date and source

acceptance.given: I select one debit
acceptance.then: the leave request it came from is shown

user_stories.want: to read an employee's balance as at a past date
user_stories.so_that: I can answer disputes about what was available when leave was applied

acceptance.given: an employee in my entity disputes a rejection on 3 August 2026
acceptance.when: I project the balance as at 3 August 2026
acceptance.then: only ledger rows effective on or before that date are counted

acceptance.given: an employee outside my entity grant
acceptance.then: the request is refused and an access event is logged

use_cases.name: Manage maternity and paternity leave
use_cases.goal: Administer statutory maternity benefit and paternity leave end to end, including medical evidence, nursing breaks and return-to-work milestones (entitlements to be validated by Legal).

stakeholders.interest: Receives the full statutory entitlement and a planned return without chasing HR.
Holds documentary evidence and dates needed for statutory registers.
Knows which days are paid by the employer and which are covered by a statutory scheme.
Plans cover for the absence period.

use_cases.trigger: An employee applies for maternity or paternity leave, or HR records a notified pregnancy or birth.
preconditions: Maternity and paternity leave types are configured with entitlement, eligibility service and evidence requirements from the effective rule pack (to be validated by Legal).
The employee holds an active assignment.
postconditions_success: The leave is APPROVED with evidence attached, ledger debits posted and a payroll input raised for paid days.
Nursing-break allowance and return-to-work milestones are scheduled on the employee's calendar.
postconditions_failure: The request remains pending with the missing evidence or eligibility condition named.

main_flow.action: Apply for maternity or paternity leave on Apply for leave, entering expected date of delivery or birth date and planned start.
Upload the medical certificate or birth evidence required by the leave type.
Check eligibility service and entitlement from the leave type and project the balance as at the start date.
Verify the evidence and confirm the dates; the request then enters the leave approval chain.
On approval, debit the ledger, mark attendance as maternity or paternity leave and raise payroll inputs for paid days.
Schedule return-to-work milestones and notify the employee and manager 14 days before the return date.
On return, confirm the return date; nursing-break minutes are applied to the attendance shift for the configured period.

alternate_flows.condition: The delivery occurs before the planned start date.
steps: HR operations updates the start date to the actual date; the platform re-projects the span and adjusts attendance and payroll inputs.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee requests an extension using EL or unpaid leave.
steps: A separate leave request is raised and validated under LVE-03; it is contiguous with the maternity span.

exception_flows.condition: The employee does not meet the eligibility service condition.
exception_flows.handling: The request is held for HR operations with the condition named; HR may record a policy exception with reason.

exception_flows.condition: Evidence is missing or illegible.
exception_flows.handling: HR operations returns the request to the employee with the reason; the approval chain does not start.

exception_flows.condition: A paid day falls inside a locked payroll period.
exception_flows.handling: The payroll effect is raised as arrears in the next open run.

nfrs: Medical evidence is stored encrypted and visible only to the employee and HR operations within scope.
Return-to-work reminders are delivered at least 14 days before the return date.

user_stories.want: to apply for maternity leave with my medical certificate in one step
user_stories.so_that: I do not have to visit HR in person

acceptance.given: I attach a medical certificate and an expected delivery date of 20 January 2027
acceptance.then: the request is created with the document linked and HR operations receives a verification task

acceptance.given: I submit without the required certificate
acceptance.then: submission is blocked with the message naming the missing evidence

user_stories.want: the span to move when the actual delivery date differs from the planned one
user_stories.so_that: attendance and payroll match what actually happened

acceptance.given: approved maternity leave starts on 10 January 2027
acceptance.when: HR records the actual delivery on 2 January 2027
acceptance.then: the span starts on 2 January and attendance from 2 January shows maternity leave

acceptance.given: the change touches a locked December run
acceptance.then: an arrears request is raised for the next open run

user_stories.want: a reminder before my team member returns
user_stories.so_that: I can plan the handover and nursing-break schedule

acceptance.given: the return date is 15 July 2027
acceptance.then: the manager and employee receive a return-to-work reminder

acceptance.given: the employee confirms return on 15 July
acceptance.when: the shift for July is read
acceptance.then: the configured nursing-break minutes appear on her attendance days

use_cases.name: Grant and close a leave of absence
use_cases.goal: Approve a long unpaid leave or sabbatical with its effects on service continuity, benefits eligibility and payroll defined in advance, and manage the return.

stakeholders.interest: Knows before leaving how the absence affects service, benefits and pay.
Stops and restarts pay on the right dates without manual holds.
Keeps service-continuity records correct for gratuity and seniority.

use_cases.trigger: An employee requests an unpaid leave of absence or sabbatical longer than the leave type's minimum duration.
preconditions: Leave-of-absence types are configured with service-continuity, benefits and payroll treatment.
postconditions_success: The absence is approved, payroll inputs suspend pay for the span, and service and benefit flags reflect the configured treatment.
A return task is scheduled for the planned return date.
postconditions_failure: The request is rejected or withdrawn; no payroll or service change is made.

main_flow.action: Request a leave of absence, selecting type (unpaid or sabbatical), dates and reason.
Show the configured effect on service continuity, benefits eligibility and pay before submission.
Route the request through the chain definition resolved for the leave-of-absence type and duration.
Approve or reject the request in sequence with comments.
On approval, raise payroll inputs suspending pay for the span and set service and benefit flags as configured.
Create a return-from-leave task for HR operations due 7 days before the planned return date.
Confirm the actual return date; the platform restores pay and benefits from that date.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee returns earlier than planned.
steps: HR operations records the actual return date; unused absence days are released and pay resumes from that date.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee does not return and resigns.
steps: HR operations closes the absence on the resignation date and starts the exit process.

exception_flows.condition: The duration exceeds the limit the chain allows at HR Head level.
exception_flows.handling: The chain definition adds the Director / approver step before approval completes.

exception_flows.condition: The span overlaps a locked payroll period.
exception_flows.handling: The pay suspension for locked dates is raised as arrears (recovery) in the next open run.

nfrs: The pay-suspension input is created within 1 minute of final approval.

user_stories.want: to see how a sabbatical affects my service and benefits before I submit
user_stories.so_that: I can decide with full information

acceptance.given: the sabbatical type is configured as service-continuous with benefits suspended
acceptance.when: I select it with dates 1 February to 31 May 2027
acceptance.then: the form states service continues, benefits are suspended and pay stops for 120 days

acceptance.given: I change the type to unpaid leave
acceptance.then: the stated effects update to the unpaid leave configuration

user_stories.want: pay to stop and restart automatically on the approved and actual return dates
user_stories.so_that: no manual hold is needed

acceptance.given: a leave of absence from 1 February to 31 May 2027 is approved
acceptance.then: the employee has zero earnings for February with the absence named as the reason

acceptance.given: HR confirms the actual return on 20 May 2027
acceptance.then: pay is computed from 20 May

use_cases.name: Donate earned leave to a colleague or shared bank
use_cases.goal: Allow an employee to transfer earned leave to a named colleague or to a pooled leave bank within policy limits and with HR approval.

stakeholders.interest: Can support a colleague facing a long illness or emergency.
Keeps donations within policy and auditable.
Donated days do not distort encashment liability.

use_cases.trigger: An employee chooses Donate leave from the balance screen.
preconditions: The leave scheme enables donation with per-donor annual limit and minimum retained balance.
postconditions_success: A donor debit and recipient (or bank) credit are written in one transaction, each referencing the other.
postconditions_failure: No ledger row is written for either party.

main_flow.action: Choose Donate leave, select a named colleague or the shared bank, and enter the number of EL days.
Check the donor's projected EL balance, the annual donation limit and the minimum balance the donor must keep.
Create a donation request and route it to HR operations for approval.
Approve or reject the donation with a comment.
On approval, write the donor debit and recipient credit in one transaction, each referencing the other.
Notify donor and recipient; the recipient's projected balance shows the credit as donated leave.

alternate_flows.condition: The donor gives to the shared bank.
steps: The credit goes to the bank; HR operations later allocates bank days to an approved recipient with a reason.

exception_flows.condition: The donation would breach the annual limit or the minimum retained balance.
exception_flows.handling: The request is blocked with the limit and the maximum permitted days shown.

exception_flows.condition: Either ledger write fails.
exception_flows.handling: Both writes roll back and the donation stays approved but unposted, with a retry offered.

nfrs: The donor's identity is shown to the recipient only if the donor opts in.

user_stories.want: to donate EL to a colleague within policy limits
user_stories.so_that: I can help them without breaching my own minimum balance

acceptance.given: my projected EL is 12, the minimum retained is 5 and the annual limit is 5
acceptance.when: I offer 5 days to a colleague
acceptance.then: the request is created and routed to HR operations

acceptance.given: the same balances
acceptance.then: the request is blocked and 5 days is shown as the maximum

user_stories.want: donor and recipient entries to be written together and linked
user_stories.so_that: the ledgers always balance

acceptance.given: a 3-day donation is approved
acceptance.then: the donor shows a 3-day debit and the recipient a 3-day credit, each referencing the other

acceptance.given: the recipient write fails
acceptance.then: neither entry exists

use_cases.name: Publish approved leave to the corporate calendar
use_cases.goal: Show approved leave as out-of-office entries on the employee's and team's corporate calendars and keep them in step with later changes.

stakeholders.interest: Does not have to create out-of-office entries by hand.
Sees team absence where meetings are planned.
Controls whether and how leave details leave the platform.

use_cases.trigger: leave.request.approved, a cancellation, an HR edit or leave.early_return.recorded.
preconditions: The tenant has connected a corporate calendar and enabled leave publishing.
The employee's calendar identity is linked through the enterprise directory.
postconditions_success: The calendar entry matches the approved span; it carries no leave type or reason.
postconditions_failure: The leave stays approved; the failed publish is retried and shown on the employee's leave record.

main_flow.action: Receive leave.request.approved for an employee whose calendar is linked.
Build an out-of-office entry with dates and half-day flags only, without leave type or reason.
Create the entry on the employee's calendar and return its reference.
Store the reference on the leave request and add the entry to the team calendar view.
On cancellation, HR edit or early return, update or delete the entry using the stored reference.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee returns early.
steps: The entry's end date is shortened to the day before the actual return date.

exception_flows.condition: The corporate calendar is unavailable.
exception_flows.handling: The publish is retried with backoff for 24 hours; the employee is then notified to add the entry manually.

exception_flows.condition: The employee has no linked calendar identity.
exception_flows.handling: No publish is attempted; the leave record shows 'Calendar not linked'.

nfrs: Calendar entry appears within 2 minutes of approval at p95.
No leave type, reason or medical detail is sent to the corporate calendar.

user_stories.want: approved leave to appear as out-of-office on my calendar
user_stories.so_that: colleagues do not book me while I am away

acceptance.given: my 2 to 4 December 2026 EL is approved and my calendar is linked
acceptance.then: an out-of-office entry for 2 to 4 December appears without the leave type

acceptance.given: I cancel the leave on 28 November
acceptance.then: the entry is removed from my calendar

user_stories.want: early returns to shorten the calendar entry
user_stories.so_that: the team calendar shows when the person is actually back

acceptance.given: an entry runs 1 to 10 October 2026
acceptance.when: an early return on 7 October is recorded
acceptance.then: the entry now ends on 6 October

acceptance.given: the corporate calendar is unavailable during the update
acceptance.when: the retry window is still open
acceptance.then: the update is retried and succeeds when the calendar recovers

use_cases.name: Choose optional and restricted holidays
use_cases.goal: Let employees pick optional or restricted holidays from a location-specific, religion-neutral list within the configured quota.

stakeholders.interest: Chooses holidays that matter to them without disclosing reasons.
Knows in advance who will be absent on each optional holiday.
Configures the list and quota per location and year.

use_cases.trigger: The optional-holiday window opens for the year, or an employee selects an optional holiday later in the year.
preconditions: The optional holiday list and quota (for example 2 per year) are configured per location for the year.
postconditions_success: The chosen holidays are recorded, the quota is reduced and attendance shows the day as optional holiday.
postconditions_failure: No selection is recorded; quota is unchanged.

main_flow.action: Publish the optional holiday list and annual quota for each location.
Show each employee the list for their work location with the remaining quota.
Select one or more optional holidays from the list.
Check the remaining quota and conflicts with rest days and approved leave.
Record the selection and mark the date as optional holiday on the work calendar for the employee.
View expected absence per optional holiday at the site.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee withdraws a selection before the date.
steps: The selection is removed and the quota is restored.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee transfers location mid-year.
steps: The new location's list applies from the transfer date; holidays already taken count against the annual quota.

exception_flows.condition: The quota is already used.
exception_flows.handling: The selection is refused with the quota and the holidays already chosen shown.

exception_flows.condition: The date is already a rest day or covered by approved leave.
exception_flows.handling: The selection is refused with the conflicting record named.

nfrs: The list labels holidays by name and date only; no religion field is captured or shown.

user_stories.want: to choose my optional holidays from my location's list
user_stories.so_that: I take the days that matter to me

acceptance.given: my site list has 6 optional holidays and a quota of 2
acceptance.then: both are recorded and my remaining quota shows 0

acceptance.given: my quota is 0
acceptance.when: I try to select a third
acceptance.then: the selection is refused with the two chosen holidays listed

user_stories.want: to see how many people will be off on each optional holiday
user_stories.so_that: I can plan shift cover

acceptance.given: 14 employees at my site selected 12 November 2026
acceptance.when: I open the site's optional holiday view
acceptance.then: 12 November shows 14 expected absences

acceptance.given: one of them withdraws the selection
acceptance.then: 12 November shows 13
